title: Does Height Matter in College Volleyball?
text:
College volleyball players vary in height, position, and playing style. This project asks whether taller players also have stronger on-court statistics, or whether height alone is a poor measure of performance.

Research question: Is player height associated with better college volleyball statistics after accounting for differences between positions?

title: Does Height Matter in College Volleyball?
text:
What will be compared
The analysis will compare height with performance measures such as:

kills and kills per set
hitting percentage
blocks and blocks per set
digs and digs per set
service aces

Position matters because a middle blocker and a libero are expected to contribute in different ways. The analysis should therefore look at the overall relationship and then examine positions separately.

title: Does Height Matter in College Volleyball?
text:
Working hypothesis
Height may be most strongly related to blocking and attacking statistics. However, a relationship between height and a statistic would not show that height causes better performance. Skill, training, playing time, team strategy, and position may also explain differences between players.

title: Does Height Matter in College Volleyball?
text:
Analysis plan

Clean the player-level data and check for missing values.
Summarize height and statistics with tables and visualizations.
Use scatterplots and correlations to examine relationships.
Compare results across playing positions.
Fit regression models that include height and position together.

The conclusion will focus on the strength and uncertainty of the evidence, not on whether height is a universal requirement for success.

title: Does Height Matter in College Volleyball?
text:
Current status
This page now includes an official NCAA 2025-season benchmark. The next step is to combine player heights, positions, and individual statistics so the project can test whether height is associated with performance within and across positions.
